Basis for Intervening:
The Citizens Utility Board of Minnesota (“CUB Minnesota”), pursuant to Rules 212 and 214 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (“FERC” or “Commission”) Rules of Practice and Procedures, 18 C.F.R. §§ 385.212 and 385.214, respectfully moves to intervene in Docket ER26-3650-000. CUB Minnesota has an interest that will be directly affected by the outcome of this proceeding. 

CUB is a nonprofit organization that represents the interests of residential customers of regulated gas and electric utilities in Minnesota. CUB aims to be a voice for Minnesotans at the Minnesota Public Utilities Commission and the state legislature, where we advocate for just, reasonable, affordable, and reliable utility service. CUB engages on a variety of dockets and issues, including those related to transmission and large load projects proposed for development in Minnesota. 

CUB has an interest in ensuring Minnesotans pay just and reasonable rates for electricity service, which includes transmission, capacity, and energy costs incurred as a result of utilities’ participation in the Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc. (“MISO”) market. The tariff changes submitted by MISO relate to the accelerated development of large loads on the midcontinent transmission system, as well as the protections and measures necessary to maintain reliability and alleviate cost-shifting concerns. The Commission’s decision in the instant proceeding will therefore influence the rates paid by Minnesotans, and CUB has an interest in such outcome. 

For these reasons, CUB’s participation in this matter is in the public interest and we respectfully request the Commission grant this motion to intervene.
